01.title: NSC gateway is re-entrant: a nested veneer call can replace the signed calldata after the confirm screen in the single-sign handler (SIGN_SNAP_BUF is re-read post-confirm)

02.title: FSBL: the signature gate admits on one skipped branch, and the boot slot is one unencoded stack word (close before the WRP + RDP-2 freeze)

04.title: Ship option-byte profile has no field for SRAM_RST (or SRAM2_RST / SRAM2_ECC / SRAM3_ECC): the first-boot self-lock would freeze the factory default, which never erases secure RAM on reset

05.title: RDP-2 burn routine is inert: OPTSTRT / OBL_LAUNCH / OPTLOCK are written to FLASH_SECCR, where they do not exist, and the routine returns Ok (split out of #268)

06.title: The verify-before-first-power check that invariant 10(a) depends on cannot be run by a buyer: tools/verify_ship_state.py hashes zero bytes of flash, has only a bench profile, and no sealed unit exposes SWD

08.title: halt_on_glitch parks in a bare wfe loop without zeroizing on a genuinely detected glitch (the part of #835 H4 that survives removing the TRNG-failure sink)

10.title: PIN entry does not hold TrustedUiWaitGuard while iwdg is in the ship set: by source read, an ordinary slow PIN entry ends in a watchdog reset

11.title: Lockout response differs by unlock arm: only the USB arm wipes on PinLocked, and a lockout raised by a secure element at the boot or idle prompt has no wipe trigger at all

13.title: No stack limit register (MSPLIM) is set in any image, and the FSBL has no NMI or ECC handler; the FSBL half can never be added after the freeze

14.title: PIN credentials are not die-bound or salted (SE050 UserID is the raw PIN, OPTIGA F1D0 is one SHA-256 of it), while the threat model says single-chip extraction is defeated

15.title: The secure-world SECBOOTADD0 check does nothing in production: its mismatch branch contains only secure_log!, which compiles to nothing without debug-log

16.title: approve(addr, 0) on a contract with no token metadata renders "Revoke approval"; on an ERC-721 contract the same call grants token 0

17.title: Seed letters and the live PIN digit are drawn through the public (address-keyed) font path on the shipping 16x4 UI, and the letter dial always starts at "a"

18.title: cmd_pin_attempt_log guards its write to a non-secure pointer with one bare branch (no FI sentinel), unlike its sibling handlers

19.title: A locked device paints the trusted PIN dialog on every host unlock request with no rate bound, and the PIN start-digit scrambler falls back to all zeros when the RNG fails

20.title: Low-severity hardening items from the 2026-10 frontier research: no jitter before the first sentinel check, cycle counter exposed to non-secure code, single-read lockout, dead internal tampers, no blank check after erase, placeholder device info

21.title: First-boot journal: ALL_DONE is committed without requiring the earlier step bits, and all_done() tests that one bit, so a step skipped by one fault is never re-run

21b.title: duress-pin: page-123 counters have no wallet discriminator, so OFFCHAIN_STATUS after a decoy unlock shows the real wallet's counts

22.title: FSBL freeze items with no issue: every FI delay is the constant 0x42, the slot tail beyond the declared lengths is never measured or checked blank, and the boot fingerprint covers the secure image only

23.title: FI and wipe assurance does not test what the docs say: fi_target does not build, the C10 verify sweep never reaches the WOTS or root compares, delay-source fixes are stranded on a branch, and the wipe-recovery e2e cannot pass since S-6

25.title: Docs and comments that describe controls or states the code does not have (ten items, 2026-10 frontier research)

26.title: Owner decision before the first user wallet: take #131 (per-key budget reset) and an optional guard hook in PQSmartWallet as one contract decision; a separate vault contract is the candidate for protecting savings

r2:H1.title: The V10 schematic puts a backup capacitor on VBAT and two crystals on the MCU, but three documents assume neither: confirm what is fitted, measure the hold time, align the docs

r2:M14.title: Lockout wipe: bound the boot-time resume, add a terminal "wipe incomplete" state, and check both secure elements for survivors before the setup wizard

r2:SE-06.title: Add an MCU-side "wallet provisioned" record as the seed-wizard gate: today the only gate is two secure-element probes that can each be forced to read "blank"

r2:FI-01.title: First on-silicon fault-injection campaign on the firmware's own gates (PIN gate, signature compare, bootloader admission): untracked legs and a receipt rule

r2:M19.title: Enrol the binary never-ship audit in CI with a two-sided control, give a red nightly a consequence, and add image-level FI and glyph-leak regression checks

r2:M11.title: Desk review of the V10 artwork for where display and button lines can be tapped, plus anti-tamper requirement fixes, before the next board is specified

r2:X2a.title: fwsign: compute each vendor-key signature twice in separate processes and compare, keep a fail-closed signature ledger, and split digest / sign / assemble

r2:X5a.title: Pixel UI reads glyphs from non-secure flash between two hash checks of it: paint from the hashed copy, and make all DMA channels secure and locked at boot

r2:X8a.title: Mark secure RAM execute-never with the secure memory protection unit, so a fault that redirects the program counter cannot run bytes the companion supplied

r2:D-07.title: Seed words stay in stack buffers after the 16x4 seed pages are drawn, and no executed test covers either display wipe (pixel-UI half already landed)

r2:SYS-06.title: Keep a small fault record across the security reset: fault-status registers in backup registers 8 to 31, read through the existing diagnostic command

r2:M17.title: Add a read-only per-boot check of OPTIGA object metadata against a pinned table: it is compared only during provisioning, so a loose chip boots normally

r2:SCA-02.title: Run the SE050 tunnel AES (SCP03 key derivation, MAC, encryption) on the SAES hardware block instead of software AES; land after the tunnel leakage measurement

r2:CS-02.title: Give Safe custody-change pages one shared danger classification: today a Safe-wrapped unlimited approve does not pulse and owner changes have plain heads

r2:CS-03.title: Design a secure-world spending-policy guard: allowlists, per-operation caps and forbid toggles checked on the decoded request before the confirm screen

r2:X6a.title: Document and test pq1 as a required owner of a k-of-n Safe on the shipped approveHash route: threat-model row, version matrix, real-Safe test

r2:IMP-09.title: Host-side check that each WOTS+C count in a device signature is the smallest valid one (closes the smaller of two firmware covert channels; R stays open)

r2:CS-04.title: Owner decision: should production builds refuse a non-empty paymaster instead of warning and signing? The device signs a hash it cannot decode (review finding H-6 has no issue)

r2:M13.title: Show two device-bound words part-way through PIN entry, so a swapped unit is noticed before the whole PIN is typed

r2:pin-03.title: Page-124 PIN attempt counter: an all-0xFF read decodes as "zero attempts"; decide on a self-checking record encoding, with an atomic reset designed first

r2:X1a.title: Design-first: opt-in restore that never draws a seed letter, entering the phrase as button bits under an on-screen one-time mask (stops a display-only tap)

r2:M10.title: Bench go/no-go study: can firmware see a logger soldered to the display lines by timing how fast each line charges? Measure first, build no detector

r2:CS-09.title: Tag a fund-destination address that equals the current wallet ("THIS WALLET"), computed in the secure world and never taken from the companion

r2:X7b.title: Show Sign-In with Ethereum (EIP-4361) messages as structured pages before the raw text, with on-device address and chain consistency checks

r2:X3a.title: Pin two gateway policy sets with source tests: the one handler that signs without a prompt (command 15) and the entries callable on a locked device

r2:H2.title: Five open checks from the 2026-10 research that no issue carries: pre-existing secure-element state at setup, two leakage measurements, a port-B pin readback, one unsourced figure
